recommendedTextbook.title: Physical and Health Education for Junior Secondary Schools Book 3
recommendedTextbook.author: A. O. Folawiyo, B. A. Miller, S. M. Oloyede
recommendedTextbook.approvedBy: NERDC & Lagos State Ministry of Basic Education

topics.topic: First Aid and Emergency Management for Sports Injuries
subtopics: Aims of First Aid (preserve life, prevent worsening, promote recovery)
Management of sprains, strains, fractures, dislocations, heat stroke, bleeding
The R.I.C.E. protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) basics
objectives: Explain the 4 steps of the R.I.C.E. treatment for acute sports sprains
Demonstrate triangular bandage immobilization of a fractured forearm
Perform simulated chest compressions and rescue breathing (CPR) on an anatomical mannequin

topics.topic: Drug Abuse in Sports: Doping and Performance Enhancing Substances
subtopics: Definition of drug abuse and sports doping
Classes of banned substances: Anabolic steroids, stimulants, beta-blockers, narcotics, diuretics, erythropoietin (EPO)
Health consequences and anti-doping regulations of WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency)
objectives: Identify 4 categories of performance-enhancing drugs banned in competitive sports
Analyze physiological damages caused by chronic anabolic steroid abuse (cardiac failure, liver damage)
State moral and disciplinary penalties imposed by WADA on cheating athletes

topics.topic: Nutrition and Athletic Performance: Balanced Diet
subtopics: The 6 classes of food nutrients and their physiological roles in exercise
Pre-event meals, carbohydrate loading, hydration strategies, post-workout recovery nutrition
Nutritional deficiency diseases: Kwashiorkor, marasmus, scurvy, rickets, anemia
objectives: Design a balanced nutritional day plan for a 15-year-old school athletics competitor
Explain why carbohydrate loading maximizes glycogen stores before endurance cross-country races
Calculate daily caloric energy requirements based on basal metabolic rate and activity levels

topics.topic: Consumer Health: Quackery, Health Insurance and Consumer Agencies
subtopics: Meaning and dangers of medical quackery and fake medicines in Nigeria
Methods of detecting counterfeit medications (NAFDAC scratch-and-verify pin)
National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS/NHIA) and consumer rights in healthcare
objectives: Identify 4 red flags that signal fraudulent medical quacks and herbal peddlers
Demonstrate using the NAFDAC Mobile Authentication Service (MAS) on medication packaging
Explain how health insurance pools risk to provide affordable medical care for Nigerian families
